logline: Three impoverished sisters stumble onto 70 billion won linked to Korea's wealthiest family, and what begins as a financial windfall spirals into a conspiracy of inheritance, betrayal, and survival.

renewal.note: Single-season limited series, 12 episodes, concluded October 9, 2022. No continuation has been announced.

bollymeter.basis: 100 percent Rotten Tomatoes from 6 critics at 8.5/10 average; 7.7 IMDb from a wider audience base; APAN Drama of the Year 2023; critics praised the thriller architecture and Kim Go-eun's lead performance while audiences tracked a meaningful dip mid-series.

seasons.review_body: Directed by Kim Hee-won and written by Jeong Seo-kyung, the team behind The World of the Married, this 12-episode tvN series aired Saturdays and Sundays from September 3 to October 9, 2022. It ranked first in its timeslot every week, with a 11.1 percent finale rating. The Rotten Tomatoes score highlights the strength of the ensemble, especially Kim Go-eun's eldest-sister lead and Uhm Ji-won's antagonist, along with the structural confidence of a thriller built around class and female agency. Entertainment Weekly included it among the top 21 Korean shows on Netflix in 2025. On IMDb, a 7.7 score aligns with a mid-series stretch where the conspiracy mechanics feel unwieldy, with episodes 7 to 9 posting the lowest individual ratings, even as the opening two episodes and the finale stand out as some of the strongest hours.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.review_body: Little Women Season 1 Episode 1 aired September 3, 2022 on tvN as the premiere of Kim Hee-won and Jeong Seo-kyung’s 12-episode thriller - the director-writer team behind The World of the Married. The series earned a perfect 100-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 6 critics averaging 8.5 out of 10, ranked first in its timeslot every week of its broadcast run, and received the APAN Drama of the Year award for 2023. The premiere earns its 8.2 IMDb episode rating by grounding the fantasy-scale stakes - 70 billion won, Korea’s wealthiest family, a conspiracy spanning decades - in granular class detail from the first scene: the three sisters’ poverty is specific and unglamorous, their different responses to it established in parallel as character rather than backstory. Oh In-joo’s discovery of the money arrives through a combination of accident and action rather than pure luck, which is the episode’s most important choice: the thriller mechanics engage without removing the sisters’ agency. Entertainment Weekly’s inclusion of the series among the top 21 Korean shows on Netflix in 2025 reflects a reputation that has grown beyond its original broadcast context.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere earns its 8.2 IMDb rating by grounding the fantasy-scale stakes in granular class detail: the sisters’ poverty is specific and unglamorous, and the discovery that changes their lives arrives not through luck but through a combination of coincidence and action. The episode’s economy keeps the story moving, delivering a lot of world-building without it feeling like exposition.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Oh In-joo discovering the money - the exact instant the thriller mechanics engage and the tone shifts from domestic drama.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 12
episode_reviews.review_body: Little Women Season 1 Episode 12 aired October 9, 2022 on tvN as the series finale and its highest-rated broadcast episode at 11.1 percent nationwide - confirming that the audience which the premiere built had followed the full arc to its conclusion. The 100-percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 6 critics encompasses the finale in a consensus that Kim Hee-won's direction and Jeong Seo-kyung's writing maintained the series' quality across twelve episodes. The IMDb audience score of 7.7 and the individual episode tracking that shows a mid-series dip (episodes 7 to 9) before recovery reflect a show whose conspiracy mechanics grew more elaborate than the runtime could fully accommodate - an acknowledged structural limitation that the finale resolves with more focus on character than on plot closure. Kim Go-eun's Oh In-joo and Uhm Ji-won's antagonist reach their final confrontation with the class-politics argument the series had been making from the premiere intact. The APAN Drama of the Year 2023 award recognised the series as a whole; the finale is the episode where the ensemble's final performances, sustained across twelve episodes of escalating pressure, justify the recognition.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale, the series' highest-rated broadcast episode at 11.1 percent nationwide, attempts to pay off a conspiracy that had grown more complex than the run time could fully accommodate. The resolution leaves some questions about whether it feels earned, but the ensemble's final performances and the class-politics throughline consistently land.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The confrontation that recontextualises whose story this actually was - a structural reversal the screenplay had planted across all twelve episodes.
